conclusion: CORRECTION OF THE GRAPH-POLYNOMIAL DEFINITIONS (pinned / unpinned / fully weighted). Let G contain the reference triangle R0,R1,R2. PINNED polynomial P_j(G;y)=sum over proper 3-colourings c with c(R_i)=i of prod_v y_v^{[c(v)=j]} (17584 uses j=1). UNPINNED colour-1 polynomial U(G;y)=sum over ALL proper colourings of prod_v y_v^{[c(v)=1]}. Every c is uniquely sigma^-1 o c' with c' pinned, hence U = sum_{sigma in S3} P_{sigma(1)} = 2(P_0+P_1+P_2). For any graph with an edge the involution swapping colours 0 and 2 is a fixed-point-free bijection on proper colourings preserving every monomial of U, so U is divisible by 2 and vanishes identically in characteristic 2: the factor 1+e_v1(y_v-1) does not distinguish colours 0,2 and is only admissible for PINNED graphs. FULLY WEIGHTED polynomial W(G;X)=sum over proper colourings prod_v prod_{c=0..2}(1-e_vc+e_vc X_vc) = sum_c prod_v X_{v,c(v)} (one-hot e). VNP: W and P are sums over e in {0,1}^{3|V|} of g=prod_v oh_v(e) * prod_{uv}(1-sum_c e_uc e_vc) * prod_v prod_c(1-e_vc+e_vc X_vc); the edge factor is 0/1-valued ONLY on one-hot e, and oh_v (=1 exactly on one-hot vectors, 0 elsewhere on {0,1}^3) kills all other e, so g is 0/1 times a weight monomial; deg g and size of g are O(|V|+|E|); W,P in VNP over every field. CORRECTION OF THE MODEL-TRANSFER STATEMENTS (T58 section D was false in one direction). Four models: (F) formal polynomial circuit over F; (E) evaluation on {0,1}-inputs of an F-circuit, i.e. an F-circuit that only has to agree with the polynomial on the cube; (S) Boolean semiring (or,and) evaluation of the polynomial with N-coefficients, i.e. monotone circuits; (B) general Boolean circuits with negation. Valid implications: F-circuit => E-circuit (same circuit). Over a FIXED finite field F_p: F-circuit of size s => Boolean circuit of size O(s log^2 p) for the F_p-valued function on Boolean inputs (arithmetic mod p simulated gate by gate). Monotone N-circuit (no subtraction, N-constants) => S-circuit via the semiring homomorphism N->B (Held-Karp for HC is of this kind). NOT valid: F-circuit => S-circuit. Counterexample: over F_2 Per_n=Det_n has polynomial-size formal circuits (division-free Berkowitz), while the Boolean-semiring evaluation of Per_n is the perfect-matching indicator whose monotone circuit size is n^{Omega(log n)} (Razborov 1985, EXTERNAL, cited from memory); subtraction/cancellation/char-2 identities have no semiring image. Lower bounds go the other way: LB(B) => LB(E over F_p) => LB(F). A formal lower bound (OpenAI) therefore implies NO Boolean-circuit or semiring lower bound; the missing step is exactly E vs F (circuits may compute g=f+sum(x_i^2-x_i)h_i). T58 statements 'formal upper bound => models 2,3 upper bound' are corrected to: => E yes; => B (finite field value) yes; => S only for monotone circuits.

PRE-CHECK + SUCCINCT TABLEAU (Meyer mechanism, contrapositive form; known technique, restated). Let M be a fixed deterministic exponential-time machine for an EXP-complete L. Call x c-succinct if the tableau function (t,i)->cell of M on x has a circuit of size <= |x|^c. If every x is c-succinct then L is in Sigma2^p: guess circuit C (size <= |x|^c), check forall (t,i) the local rules, the initial row = x and read the acceptance cell; determinism makes a locally consistent C equal to the true tableau. Hence P=NP (Sigma2=P) => EXP=P, contradicting the deterministic time hierarchy, so under P=NP: for every c there is an input x that is not c-succinct (an incompressible computation history). The compressibility needed for the pre-check route is therefore REFUTED under P=NP, not derivable from it; per-instance succinctness (circuit may depend on x) is weaker than EXP in P/poly but yields the same Sigma2 upper bound. No contradiction. ## Interpretation

A general transition function on \(k\) state bits and one input bit has a direct truth-table implementation of size \(O(k^2 2^k)\): for each output bit, OR together the input minterms on which that bit is 1. Each minterm takes \(O(k)\) fan-in-two gates, and there are at most \(2^{k+1}\) minterms per output. This is a constructive bound, but it is exponential in the state length.

This bound applies to arbitrary finite transition functions. It does not exploit the structure of EXT residuals and does not give a polynomial-size transition circuit for them. The provided finite check for S1074 covers only \(N\le3\); it is not a general proof or a transition-cost result.

Thm 4.1: rho(a+b)<=rho_a+rho_b, rho(a o b)<=rho_a*rho_b, rho(a o a)<=rho_a(rho_a+1)/2 (symmetric lift, = T66 Thm 8.1), shift and decimation keep rho (M->M^k); proof by block-diagonal, Kronecker mixed-product and Sym^2 restriction, valid over any commutative ring (bound on representation dimension, not Hankel rank). Numerics (finite tests): 64 random pairs over F_p orders 1..8, 0 violations, square rank = r(r+1)/2 for r=2,4,6,8. Not novel mathematics (weighted-automaton / Kronecker algebra); the contribution is the unification and the admission rule for a vectorised engine.
